papers.title: Social Interaction Breaks Replicate Independence in Controlled-Clone LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM evaluations and social simulations create many agents from one model and treat them as independent replicates, even after the agents interact. This assumption remains untested with matched controls. We introduce SocCogEval, a controlled-clone assay for Social Cognitive Transfer (SCT). Clones share the base model, system prompt, and decoding parameters and differ only in a private brief, and a factorial protocol separates the brief, 30 rounds of interaction, and initialization noise. On Qwen3-122B-FP8, interaction with the briefs held fixed raises off-topic BFI-10 response-profile drift by $\barΔ=+0.917$ and $+0.912$ in two topically disjoint scenarios (exact $p=0.0008$ and $0.0039$). The drift is larger than under the brief alone, persists under temperature-zero re-probing, and stays positive without typed memory extraction in exploratory tests. Matched solo generation reproduces part of it, and social interaction remains highest. Across five more model variants, every scenario-averaged interaction contrast is positive. Each interacting population is therefore one replicate, and treating its agents as independent requires paired no-interaction controls. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/koanatakiyo/SocCogEval.

papers.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
papers.abstract: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

papers.title: Neighbourhood flood damage amplifies mortgage default cascades
papers.abstract: Floods threaten mortgage repayment by damaging homes, disrupting incomes, and worsening conditions in surrounding neighbourhoods. However, it remains unclear how these neighbourhood effects turn local damage into systemic mortgage distress, as Europe's housing crisis leaves households that lose their homes with few affordable alternatives. Using an agent-based model calibrated to Limburg, the Netherlands, we show that damage to surrounding properties can trigger mortgage defaults among households that can still afford to pay, including those whose own homes remain undamaged. In the most severe flood scenario, the annual foreclosure rate more than doubles. As each foreclosure lowers the value of nearby homes, it triggers a cascade. Floods make such large foreclosure cascades more frequent, with the share of foreclosures that belong to these cascades rising from 31% to 45%. They also shift foreclosures towards younger mortgages, when more debt is still outstanding. These findings show how neighbourhood damage extends mortgage risk beyond directly flooded homes and causes foreclosures to arrive in concentrated waves earlier in repayment.

papers.title: What the annual energy balance hides: the coordination value of digital platforms for positive energy districts
papers.abstract: Positive energy districts (PEDs) are usually assessed by annual net energy, whereas distribution networks operate hour by hour. An annually positive district still imports on low-generation hours and exports or curtails on high-generation hours. How large this hourly imbalance is behind an annual balance, and how much of it coordination among prosumers can close without new physical capacity, is not established. This paper models a multi-carrier prosumer community coupling electricity and heat behind a shared grid connection with a net-export hosting limit. The model is solved as a centralized community problem and as a price-taking peer-to-peer (P2P) market. Under convexity, the equilibrium implements the regularized community optimum and the P2P and congestion prices are the duals of the pool-clearing and hosting constraints. The model is calibrated to six European district archetypes with constructed hourly profiles. Hourly self-sufficiency is only 48-50% in the four deeply studied districts and ranges from 48-55% across all six, leaving a no-platform coordination gap of 2.8-5.9% of no-platform economic cost. The shared-forecast step recovers only 6-18% of the gap, while grid-aware pricing reduces curtailment by 45% in the primary district. Coordination mainly reduces surplus-side inefficiency, whereas closing the deficit side requires storage. The results are scenario-based projections for calibrated archetypes, and the operating benefit is small and contingent on binding hosting limits and high feed-in remuneration. For regulators and distribution system operators this supports hourly, bidirectional indicators alongside the annual positive-energy target, and a congestion charge active only in binding hours with a predetermined refund, while the business case for a platform at district scale rests on grid-side value and aggregation across districts.
